page: The Microsoft Azure D16as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is allocated 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU supports boost speeds up to 4.5 GHz alongside per-core cache allocations of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, hardware AES, VAES, and SHA extensions for cryptographic tasks. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark data demonstrates exceptionally strong single-core performance. In stress-ng single-core tests, the D16as_v7 reaches the top 10% tier with a score of 3767.78, mirrored in data processing tasks where single-threaded gzip compression hits 41.61 GB/s and bzip3 decompression achieves 18.34 GB/s. PassMark memory testing registers in the upper quartile with a score of 2797.39, supported by large-block read and write bandwidths of 51.11 GB/s and 34.21 GB/s respectively. Multi-threaded execution aligns with the median tier across general cloud servers, reflecting an aggregate stress-ng multi-core score of 30076.66 and a PassMark CPU score of 33162.55.

The compute profile shows solid resource density for general enterprise computing, balancing high per-thread burst speeds with standard memory allocation. A primary operational tradeoff is the total lack of ephemeral local storage, requiring network-attached remote disks for all persistent filesystem operations. In machine learning workloads, while small parameter models (135M) perform strongly on CPU vector registers, larger models (70B) demonstrate significant throughput bottlenecks.

The D16as_v7 is well suited for medium-scale web application serving, backend microservices, caching tiers like Redis (achieving 27.12 million operations per second), relational and document databases, and continuous integration pipelines requiring rapid single-thread build times.
description: The Microsoft Azure D16as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 64.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions, but contains no discrete GPUs and zero bundled local storage, requiring external managed disks. Benchmarks show upper-decile single-core CPU execution and single-threaded data compression, alongside upper-quartile memory performance. Multithreaded operations, static web delivery, and database transactions perform within median industry ranges. The instance provides an efficient profile for enterprise web serving, Redis caching nodes, microservice backends, and CI/CD pipelines needing robust per-thread compute throughput.
